St John's Breakfast and After School Clubs
St John's Breakfast and After School Clubs
St John's Breakfast and After School Clubs
Parent information
We are primarily located in the community room at the front of the school
Breakfast Club runs from 8.00am to start of school and includes breakfast (Children need to arrive by 8.20am if they are taking breakfast) Price from 1st September 2023: £5.50 per session
After School Club runs from end of school to 6.00pm and includes a light tea. Price from 1st September 2023: £16.00 per session (Please try to be prompt in picking up your child. Extra charges may be incurred if after 6.00pm)
Miss Kan - Playleader
Miss Knight - Play Assistant
Mrs Sandalls - Play Assistant
Mrs Dearlove - Play Assistant
Mrs Edwards - Play Assistant
Mrs Dasari - Play Assistant
We always have creative crafts on offer as well as a range of games and fun toys to suit all age ranges in our club (4-7 years)
Breakfast/After School Club Snack:
Our Breakfast and After School Club snack menu is designed by our school cook, Mrs Sandalls, and we aim to cater for all dietary requirements.
At After School Club we offer a varied menu which includes fruit, vegetables, savoury snacks plus cakes and biscuits. Water and squash is available to drink.
Please bear in mind that children eat their afternoon snack in the dining room and then weather permitting, may play outside. If you wish to collect your child early, and before the club is back in the community room, please call the mobile number
Breakfast & After School Club Mobile Number: 07849 162860
Please note that there is no parking for parents at any time on school grounds, unless you have prior agreement from the Executive Headteacher
Breakfast and After School Club charges are reviewed every September
Up to 24 places are available each day for children of St John's School in our Breakfast and After School Clubs, although currently our breakfast club is capped at 16 children.
For further details or to book please email finance@stjohnandstnicolasschools.org.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: St Nicolas School's Learning Behaviours | St John and St Nicolas Schools Federation
pageCache.text:
St Nicolas School's Learning Behaviours
We strongly believe that when children have the correct attitude to learning, they always excel. We regularly talk to the children about having the right attitude and we always try to praise effort and attitude in class, rather than results. We do a lot of work, both in class and in assembly, about having the right learning behaviour. We talk with the children about the different learning behaviours that we have and encourage them to have a growth mindset – never saying, ‘I can’t do this’… but always saying, ‘I can’t do this YET’.
Across the school, we have five different learning behaviours that we focus on so that we can become the best learners that we can be. Each of our learning behaviours is represented by an animal and uses a chosen colour. This helps us to remember them all. We have created a list of what each learning behaviour looks like and we regularly talk about this in class and in our assemblies. This success criteria can be seen on the sheet at the bottom of this page and it can be downloaded for people to use at home. Our learning behaviours are promoted through posters which can be seen around the school and each learning behaviour has a story that accompanies it to support all our pupils to understand them.
Rewarding Good Learning Behaviour
When the children show good learning behaviour, they receive a house point tick on their class board. Each week, the house achieving the most points is celebrated in assembly and are rewarded with a cup. At the end of each term, the house with the highest accumulated points earns a non-school uniform day for all the children in that house.
We would like all parents to support us at home with our learning behaviours. Parents can talk about the learning behaviour with their child and should praise their child when they see that they are showing it. Parents should be role models themselves and can help their child know clearly what each learning behaviour is all about. By continually showing all five learning behaviours, our children become the very best learners that they can be.

Tier 2 words are high-frequency words that children are likely to come across in many different subjects and texts. They are not as basic as everyday words (like dog or happy) and not as technical as subject-specific vocabulary (like photosynthesis). Instead, Tier 2 words (such as investigate, prefer or fortunate) help children develop richer language for speaking, reading and writing.
The FFT scheme we use at St John’s incorporates Tier 2 vocabulary, helping children develop the rich and versatile language they need for reading and writing across the curriculum. This supports children in building a strong foundation of words that they will encounter frequently in many different contexts.
At St Nic’s, we have specially selected 10 Tier 2 words for each English unit we teach, so that children can continue to build a strong and useful vocabulary.
Here are the lists of Tier 2 vocabulary for each year group:
What are Reading VIPERS?
At St Nic’s, we use Reading VIPERS to help children develop their understanding of what they read.
VIPERS is an acronym that stands for the six key skills of reading comprehension:
V – Vocabulary: understanding the meaning of words
I – Inference: reading between the lines to understand what is implied
P – Prediction: thinking about what might happen next
E – Explanation: explaining preferences, opinions and reasons
R – Retrieval: finding information directly from the text
S – Sequence or Summarise: ordering events or summarising main ideas.
Children become confident in answering different types of questions.
Teachers can check which skills children find easier or harder.
Lessons can then be adapted to give targeted support.

How you can support at home
When reading with your child, you can use VIPERS to guide you when asking your child questions about what they are reading.
Vocabulary
Help your child explore word meanings.
What does this word mean?
Can you think of another word that means the same?
Which word tells us the character is feeling worried?
Inference
Encourage your child to think about what is implied.
Why do you think the character did that?
How do you know the animal is frightened?
What impression do you get of this setting?
Prediction
Talk about what might happen next.
What do you think will happen in the next chapter? Why?
Look at the title — what do you think the story will be about?
Explanation
Give children the chance to explain ideas.
Who is your favourite character? Why?
How does the author build tension here?
Why has the text been set out in this way?
Retrieval
Practise finding information in the text.
Where did the story take place?
What year did the astronauts land on the moon?
Who was the first character we met?
Sequence / Summarise
Encourage retelling or summarising.
What happened at the beginning, middle and end?
Can you put these events in the right order?
Can you summarise the story in a few sentences?

Late/Absence Procedures
Punctuality is really important. The first few minutes of the school day set the tone for the day.
St John's School starts at 8.45am. Gates are opened at 8.40am and closed promptly at 8.50am to ensure children's safety. If you arrive after 8.50am, you should bring your child to the school office.
St Nic's School starts promptly at 9am and again the gates are shut at this time. Any child arriving after this time should go to the office.
If your child is absent, it is really important to let the school know each day that they are away. Please phone or email the school to let us know the reason:
St John's: 01635 41281 office@stjohnev.w-berks.sch.uk
St Nic's: 01635 41282 office@stnics.w-berks.sch.uk

pageCache.text:
Music
Music Curriculum at St John and St Nicolas Schools
In our schools, we use Charanga as the basis of our music curriculum. Charanga is a published scheme, which allows non-specialist teachers to deliver effective music teaching to all children.
In addition to this, we offer multiple opportunities across both schools for children to engage with and develop musically. This includes music tuition in several different instruments. Our music tuition is run by outside teachers from Berkshire Maestros and Good Vibes Music.
In both schools, there are opportunities for singing throughout the curriculum including in music lessons, collective worship, drama and musical productions and choirs. Each year, St Nicolas School takes part in Young Voices at the O2 Arena, taking a choir of nearly half the school to participate in this massed choir event.
